intended_object: The group homomorphism GL_S(S ⊗_R M) → Aut(Proj(Sym_R M) ×_{Spec R} Spec S): an S-linear automorphism of the base-changed coordinate module gives the induced projective linear automorphism of the base-changed projective scheme. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: The body composes `symmetricAlgebraAut S` with conjugation by `symmetricAlgebraBaseChangeIso R S M`. `symmetricAlgebraAut S` sends e to projective pullback along e⁻¹ on Proj(Sym_S(S⊗M)); using e⁻¹ makes the map covariant, and its map_mul' proof checks this against Aut's composition convention. `symmetricAlgebraBaseChangeIso` is the canonical isomorphism Proj(Sym_S(S⊗_R M)) ≅ Proj(Sym_R M) ×_{Spec R} Spec S, built from Sym_S(S⊗_R M) ≅ S⊗_R Sym_R M and Proj base change. Conjugating by it transports the linear action to the fiber product, which is exactly the intended action of GL(M_S) on P(M)_S. The file also proves that these automorphisms commute with the projection to Spec S. The setting is fully general: R and S are arbitrary commutative rings, S is any R-algebra, and M is any module, with no finiteness or flatness assumptions. Requiring R, S and M to share a universe is only a technical restriction of the scheme API. I found no Mathlib counterpart.
